title: Number of Integers With Popcount-Depth Equal to K II
summary: Given an integer array nums, for each query, determine the count of indices within a specified range where the popcount-depth matches a given value.
statement: Given an integer array nums, for each query, determine the count of indices within a specified range where the popcount-depth matches a given value. Queries can also update an element in the array. The popcount-depth of an integer x is the minimum number of steps to reach 1 by repeatedly applying the popcount function, which counts the number of 1s in the binary representation of x.
constraints: Up to 100,000 positive values and queries.
Type one counts a requested depth in an inclusive index range; type two updates one value.
Depth is between zero and five.
hints: Only six depth categories exist, so maintain one frequency structure per category.
Use six Fenwick trees for range counts and point updates.
Remove the old depth, compute and add the new depth, and answer with prefix differences.
Each tree exactly tracks indices in one category, so their range sums remain correct after every update.
editorial: Each tree exactly tracks indices in one category, so their range sums remain correct after every update.

tests.explanation: The two initial powers of two have depth one; after updating, one value has depth zero.
The query answers are three, one, and zero.
